findings.title: The new decimals() staticcall copies unbounded return data and forwards all remaining gas, so a registered token can make toStableAmount - and therefore every annihilation of that pair - cost more gas than a block allows
findings.mergeAction: 2-way. PATTERN-MR-001 was routed by the pattern tier as a NON-MATCH on READ-ONLY-REENTRANCY, but its residual (b) - 'the staticcall forwards all remaining gas with no stipend (63/64 rule), so a registered token can burn the caller's gas' - is the identical mechanism CODE-203 measures. CODE-203 is the strongest framing (it carries the measurement and two passing PoCs); PATTERN-MR-001 is folded in as corroboration, not deleted.
findings.rootCause: `(bool ok, bytes memory data) = stable.staticcall(...)` at :292 allocates and RETURNDATACOPYs the callee's ENTIRE return buffer BEFORE `data.length != 32` is evaluated at :293. Memory expansion is quadratic and the call forwards all remaining gas with no stipend. Introduced by this delta: at 0bb82d8 toStableAmount made no call to `stable` at all.
findings.impact: DoS, fails closed, no theft and no burn (the revert precedes _burn at :239). (a) annihilate() is dead for that pair because :230 routes through toStableAmount; (b) toStableAmount is `public view` and the NatSpec added by this same delta at :278-279 nominates it as an off-chain quote helper, so eth_call quoting dies too.
findings.evidence: PROVEN - workspace/antimatter/test/audit/Tier2Delta.t.sol::test_returndataBombGasCost (16,782 gas for a 32-byte answer; 1,815,823 for 640KB; 158,677,386 for 6.4MB) and ::test_returndataBombBricksQuote (out-of-gas under a 30,000,000 cap against 64MB).
findings.reachability: Requires an owner-registered `stable` (StablecoinNotRegistered at :285 correctly runs FIRST). The realistic path is an upgradeable registered token whose implementation changes AFTER registration - outside the owner's control, so this is NOT an owner-misuse suppression under Law 3.
findings.recommendation: Read exactly one word and ignore the rest (assembly staticcall with a 32-byte output buffer plus an explicit returndatasize() == 32 check), and/or cap forwarded gas (e.g. {gas: 30000}). The stated reason for preferring a raw staticcall over try/catch (:289-291) remains valid and is unaffected.
findings.pocProvenance: AUDIT-AUTHORED, workspace only. NOT present in lib/antimatter @ c91bc1a. Never cite as project test coverage; never file the test path as a project file.

findings.title: Annihilation now hard-depends on every registered stablecoin answering decimals() through a static call; a token that cannot, or stops, permanently strands that pair's reward entitlement while the minter's own path keeps working
findings.mergeAction: 4-way consolidation on ONE root cause with THREE enumerated triggers. Verified before collapsing that all four cite the same defect at the same lines and share one mitigation family (registration checklist + NatSpec scope + a second registered stablecoin). SA-004 is the static seed - its own note states the substantive question is 'not the call's safety but its CONSEQUENCE', which is this finding verbatim. ECON-008 supplies the strongest framing (economic consequence + Law-3 footgun analysis) and is kept as the primary narrative.
findings.rootCause: toStableAmount fails closed on anything that is not exactly a 32-byte static-callable answer matching the minter's registered value, and it sits on annihilate's critical path (:230). The minter itself never asks the token (it reads its own config.decimals at PhusdStableMinter.sol:254), so the dependency exists ONLY on the Antimatter path.

triggerInventory.detail: Upgradeable proxy (USDC is one) ships an implementation where decimals() reverts or is dropped, while transfer/transferFrom keep working.

Owner registers a pre-EIP-20-metadata token with no decimals(). annihilate never works for it, silently, from day one - the minter supplied decimals at registration and nothing else on the mint path asks the token.

triggerInventory.trigger: T3 - honest token whose decimals() is not view-callable
triggerInventory.detail: decimals() that increments a counter, lazily caches, or emits an event returns ok == false under STATICCALL and is rejected DecimalsUnavailable even though its registration is correct and its answer would have matched.

findings.impact: Availability, not principal. The revert is in toStableAmount BEFORE _burn (:239) and before any transfer, so nothing is consumed or stranded on-chain and no attacker profits. What is lost is the ability to realise the reward leg of already-distributed antimatter against that stablecoin. Antimatter is inert when held alone: its entire value is the `amount` of unbacked phUSD annihilation emits at :260. If the bricking token is the only registered stablecoin, the whole distributed entitlement is unrealisable until the owner registers a replacement. The fault is INVISIBLE on the protocol's main minting path (PhusdStableMinter.mint for the same token is unaffected), so monitoring on the mint path shows the protocol healthy.
findings.law3Note: FOOTGUN, in scope. A competent non-malicious owner registering a stablecoin would reasonably assume the minter's own registered `decimals` field is the authority; the connection between 'this token's metadata implementation changed' and 'the reward leg is unrealisable for every holder of this pair' is not obvious from either contract. Surprise => footgun => report. NOT an owner-misuse suppression.
findings.severityRationale: Not Medium because protocol function is only partially and recoverably impaired (stable is a free parameter of annihilate, the owner can register an alternative, and no third party controls the trigger). Not QA because a real, already-distributed reward entitlement becomes unrealisable for as long as the condition persists. Severity-classifier to adjudicate the compound sole-registered-stablecoin case.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: If accepted rather than fixed, the protocol acquires an operational invariant that exists nowhere in CLAUDE.md or the NatSpec today: at least two registered stablecoins with independent metadata implementations, plus liveness monitoring on toStableAmount per registered stable. Add non-view/absent decimals() to the stablecoin-registration checklist, and widen the DecimalsUnavailable NatSpec from 'does not report usable decimals at all' to 'does not report usable decimals through a static call'.
findings.intentionalityNote: The fail-closed design is almost certainly deliberate and is arguably the right call. The finding is the undocumented operational dependency it creates, not the check's presence.

findings.title: The new exact-equality quote check is a tautology on any honest minter, yet its comment and error name present it as protection against being short-changed - which risks a future reader believing ledger F-01 has been fixed when it has not
findings.rootCause: expectedForStable (:234) and the minter's own phUSDAmount (PhusdStableMinter.sol:212) are the SAME pure view, called with identical arguments, in the same transaction, against the same owner-only-mutable config storage. They agree by construction whenever the minter behaves as written, so the check is a no-op on 100% of the honest path. The comment at :232-233 ('a short mint cannot pass unnoticed') and the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch both read as a slippage / short-mint guard. They are not one: there is no caller-supplied minimum, and an owner who lowers exchangeRate mid-flight still settles the annihilation at the new rate BECAUSE THE CHECK RE-QUOTES AT THE NEW RATE TOO.
findings.impact: No asset impact. The hazard is a FALSE-CLOSURE TRIPWIRE: ledger F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060, open) recommended asserting mintedForStable against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount), and c91bc1a implements that recommendation verbatim (see F-04.additionalContext.reObservations). A future run reading the diff alone would reasonably propose F-01 fixed. It is not: submission-time price risk on an irreversible burn is untouched.
findings.failureScenario: Owner calls minter.updateExchangeRate(usdc, 0.5e18) while Alice's annihilate(usdc, alice, 100e18) is pending. Alice lands at the new rate: 100 AM burned, 100 USDC pulled, 150 phUSD delivered instead of 200. expectedForStable (50e18) == mintedForStable (50e18), so PhUSDAmountMismatch does not fire and the code reports success.
findings.whyNotCollapsedIntoF01: Distinct root causes and distinct mitigations. F-01 is the ABSENCE of a caller-side floor (fix: add `uint256 minPhUSDOut` to annihilate). This is the PRESENCE of documentation and an error name that overstate what the new guard covers (fix: reword :232-233). Under the standing principle that falsely-exhaustive in-source docs raise rather than lower severity, and because this entry's whole function is to stop F-01 being closed on false evidence, collapsing it into F-01 would destroy the very signal it carries. Recorded as a relationship, not a merge.
findings.intentionalityNote: The check has real (if narrow) value as a defence against a FUTURE minter whose mint() diverges from its own quote. The finding is the overstated framing, not the check's presence.
findings.recommendation: Either (i) reword :232-233 to state what the check actually covers ('the minter's mint() must agree with its own calculateMintAmount(); this is NOT a slippage guard'), or (ii) close F-01 properly by adding a minPhUSDOut parameter and checking `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260.

findings.title: PhusdStableMinter's daily phUSD issuance cap governs only half the phUSD an annihilation issues: a cap of X permits 2X
findings.verdict: STILL LIVE AT c91bc1a - re-proven, not re-filed
findings.adjudication: PATTERN-001 (MINT-ON-DEMAND-OVERMINT) is M-03's root cause verbatim: the antimatter half at :260 is minted on Antimatter's own IFlax authorisation and never touches mintedToday, so an owner who sets maxMintPerDay gets approximately half the bound configured. rootCauseClass IssuanceCapCoversOnlyOneMintLeg matches exactly. Tier-3 invariant_9 measures it precisely ('charged to cap 332000000000000, actually issued 664000000000000 - exactly 2x'); invariant_8 measures the same defect in window-aggregate form (10070203377041423804312 issued > maxMintPerDay 10000000000000000000000). Neither is a new finding.
findings.whyM03AndNotM05: Deliberate single-entry mapping, reasoned rather than assumed. M-03 (df5c16e2238a3c1c, IssuanceCapCoversOnlyOneMintLeg) is UNDER-COUNTING: the cap is mis-sized because one of the two mint legs is not charged to it. M-05 (6a6a6bcba7b0dff1, SharedDailyBudgetAsymmetricExtraction) is BUDGET CONTENTION: annihilation and ordinary on-ramp minting draw on ONE budget and annihilation extracts 2x per unit of it, making griefing the on-ramp the most profitable use of the budget. PATTERN-001's description, preconditions and missingMitigations speak ONLY to the un-metered second leg; it says nothing about contention with the on-ramp or about extraction efficiency. It therefore maps to M-03 alone. M-05 is NOT closed, NOT re-filed, and NOT collapsed into M-03 - it remains a separate live wont-fix entry, and invariant_8's window-aggregate framing corroborates it as a second-order consequence (recorded in ledgerCrossReferences below).
findings.econConfirmation: econ-findings deltaAssessments M-03 and M-05 both return direction NEUTRAL with 'no re-file, no re-escalation', independently confirming the delta changed nothing here: the cap is a REVERT not a haircut (PhusdStableMinter.sol:221), so a cap event aborts inside minter.mint at :251 and can never surface as a PhUSDAmountMismatch, and calculateMintAmount reads only exchangeRate and decimals and cannot encode the cap.
findings.proposedLedgerAction: NONE. Entry remains wont-fix. Update lastSeenRun to antimatter-02 and record the two invariant counterexamples as re-proof evidence. No status change is proposed and none may be applied without a human.

findings.proposedRewordedTitle: mintedForStable is a balance delta, not an attribution: the unattributed window [:244, :256] is now enforced by exact equality, so any phUSD arriving mid-call reverts the entire annihilation instead of being mis-forwarded
findings.mergeAction: 3-way consolidation onto ONE ledger entry. All three describe the identical window and the identical mechanism - an unattributed balance delta at :256 compared for exact equality at :257 - and all three independently nominate L-01 as the match (CODE-202.relatedLedger, ECON-009.possibleDuplicateOf, PATTERN-MR-003.residualQuestion). findings.verdict: ROOT CAUSE UNCHANGED, IMPACT INVERTED. RE-WORD, DO NOT CLOSE.
findings.adjudication: The root cause named by L-01 - :256 is `_phUSD.balanceOf(this) - phUSDBefore`, an UNATTRIBUTED delta - survives the delta byte-for-byte. What changed is only what the code DOES with a mis-attributed value: at 0bb82d8 it was silently forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient (value leak); at c91bc1a exact equality reverts the whole annihilation (liveness lever). That is one finding whose impact inverted, NOT a fix plus a new finding. Closing L-01 would lose the surviving root cause, which is precisely what the econ scanner warned against (parkedForVisibleFollowUp: 'The entry should be re-worded rather than closed - closing it would lose the surviving unattributed-delta root cause').

findings.title: toStableAmount is a decimals-only rescale and is not a phUSD preview; the local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals()

findings.adjudication: Both halves of Q-01 survive verbatim, so this is a duplicate and not a new finding. But the delta makes it materially worse in three specific ways, each of which should be recorded on the existing entry rather than filed fresh: (1) the same function now holds THREE distinct decimals notions in scope at once - the shadowing local `decimals` (minter-registered), `actualDecimals` (token-reported, :294), and the still-shadowed inherited ERC20.decimals() (this token's own 18); (2) the shadowed local now propagates into an ABI-VISIBLE parameter via the new error DecimalsMismatch(address,uint8,uint256); (3) the new NatSpec at :278-279 ('Off-chain callers using this as a quote helper therefore depend on `stable` being responsive') POSITIVELY ENDORSES using toStableAmount as a quote helper - precisely the misreading Q-01 warned about - while still not saying what it does NOT quote (it never touches exchangeRate).
findings.principleApplied: In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority, and falsely-exhaustive in-source docs raise rather than lower severity. The new NatSpec therefore aggravates Q-01; it does not resolve it. Renaming the local is now a genuine comprehension fix, not a style nit.
findings.severityNote: Held at QA. The aggravation is real but the substance is still readability plus a misleading doc, with no asset or availability impact. Recorded so the severity-classifier can adjudicate rather than inheriting a stale QA label unexamined.

The pattern tier independently ruled FEE-ON-TRANSFER-ACCOUNTING a NON-MATCH on three grounds: (1) the credited amount IS the measured delta at :256, satisfying the pattern's own notVulnerableWhen literally; (2) the stable leg fails CLOSED - Antimatter approves and the minter pulls the full stableAmount, so a fee-skimming token leaves the pull short and reverts, and any residue is caught by StableNotDeposited at :254; (3) the token set is owner-registered on the minter, not open.
The econ tier separately declined to file the phUSD-side variant on the same C4 ground (phUSD is first-party FlaxToken v2 with no fee).
The static tier that raised it labelled it PRESUMPTIVELY INVALID in its own note.
argumentsAgainstBlanketInvalidity: USDT IS an explicit carve-out on this engagement - the C4 known-invalid entry reads 'Non-standard/weird ERC-20 tokens (EXCEPT USDT)'. USDT has a fee mechanism that is currently set to zero but is owner-enablable on the token contract. An adjudicator must confirm the fail-closed argument holds for USDT specifically before invoking the known-invalid carve-out, rather than disposing of the whole class in one move.
USDT is a plausible member of the registered stablecoin set for this protocol.

findings.recommendedAdjudication: Confirm the fail-closed chain (:246 pull short -> minter's pull reverts, and/or StableNotDeposited at :254 fires) holds for USDT with a non-zero fee enabled. If it holds, dispose as C4 known-invalid WITH that reasoning recorded. If it does not, this becomes a live finding and must be re-filed at honest severity, not suppressed under the fee-on-transfer heading.

findings.title: Verified false-positive / inert / Law-3-inventory static results on src/Antimatter.sol - disposed on the record, not by silence
findings.mergeAction: 9-way consolidation of NON-findings into one auditable disposition record. This collapses no root causes because none of these carries one; each is itemised individually below with its own disproof, so every input id remains independently reachable. Direct precedent: run-01's removedWithReason block, which disposed of the same detector families on the same contract.

items.reason: The multiply-after-divide IS the deliberate exactness round-trip guard producing AmountNotRepresentable. Removing it would introduce the very bug the detector warns about. Run-01 disposed of the identical result (its SA-003) with a HALMOS PROOF that the guard is sound: for every uint256 amount, if toStableAmount returns s then s * scale == amount exactly. Machine-checked, not asserted. Unchanged in substance; only the line numbers moved (255->298).

Benign by construction and disproven three ways: address(0) has no code so the staticcall returns ok=true with empty data, data.length != 32 holds, and it reverts DecimalsUnavailable(address(0)); it is also unreachable with an unregistered stable because yieldStrategy == address(0) at :285 reverts StablecoinNotRegistered first; and the project's own test_toStableAmountRevertsOnCodelessStable (test/Annihilation.t.sol:531) covers exactly this.

Intentional tuple destructuring of minter.stablecoinConfigs; 5 of 7 fields genuinely unused. Run-01 disposed of the identical result (its SA-005) the same way. NOTE CARRIED FORWARD, not re-filed: the 7-slot destructure is an ABI-COUPLING HAZARD - if the minter ever reorders or inserts a struct field there is no compile error on either side. Not a finding at the observed trees; recorded so it is not lost.

nonReentrant is not the first modifier on rescueERC20, so onlyOwner runs outside the guard. Correct in the abstract, inert here: onlyOwner is a pure storage read with no external call, so nothing can re-enter between the two modifiers. Style only. Identical disposition to run-01 SA-007.

Generic Ownable-surface enumeration. Law 3: the owner is trusted for knowing actions and malicious-owner vectors are not filed - such findings are pure noise in a self-audit. Retained ONLY as inventory. CRITICALLY: nothing a competent owner would be SURPRISED by is suppressed here - every non-obvious footgun in the enumerated setters is filed separately (DEDUP-02-002 registration liveness, DEDUP-02-005 ownership transfer, DEDUP-02-008 hook-token brick, DEDUP-02-006/007 the cap and pricing footguns on the ledger). The pattern tier reached the identical verdict independently (CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN: SUPPRESSED - Law 3).

Reframed by the static tier as a coverage question ('is any mint entry point missing the modifier?') and ANSWERED, not assumed: exactly one _mint site and exactly one _burn site exist in src/Antimatter.sol, and Tier-3 INV1 SOLE-BURN PASSED on forge AND medusa this run (65,013 medusa calls, 32,768 forge handler calls). No unguarded mint entry point exists.
Disproven arithmetically: scale = 10 ** (18 - decimals) at :297 and decimals > 18 already reverts UnsupportedDecimals at :286, so scale is in [1, 1e18] and can never be zero.

Tokens that revert on zero-value transfers are weird-ERC20 behaviour, a C4 known-invalid class. Independently mooted in annihilate by the ZeroAmount check at :222 plus the AmountNotRepresentable exactness guard, which together prevent a zero stableAmount. Flagged to the validity-checker alongside DEDUP-02-012 so the known-invalid disposal is applied by the agent that owns it - this record does NOT assert the class disposal, it applies the in-code mooting.

rescueERC20 sweeps an arbitrary token to an arbitrary recipient, but the contract holds no accounted balances by design (NatSpec :304-305: annihilate settles whole or not at all), so there is no accounting for a sweep to break. Overlaps SA-009 as owner surface.

findings.assertion: Nothing in this record was removed for being inconvenient, low-confidence, or untidy. Every item carries an affirmative disproof, an in-code mooting, or an explicit Law-3 basis. Any item whose disposal rests on a C4 known-invalid class rather than a disproof (SA-012) is additionally routed to the validity-checker.

flaggedForReview.item: DEDUP-02-001 vs DEDUP-02-002 - KEPT SEPARATE, deliberately
flaggedForReview.question: Both are new liveness dependencies created by the same new staticcall at :292, and a report-writer may want one submission. They are NOT one finding: DEDUP-02-001's root cause is the UNBOUNDED RETURNDATA COPY plus unmetered gas forwarding (fix: 32-byte assembly output buffer and/or a gas cap - a code change), while DEDUP-02-002's is the FAIL-CLOSED METADATA DEPENDENCY itself (fix: registration checklist, NatSpec scope, a second registered stablecoin - an operational change). A token that answers decimals() correctly in 32 bytes still triggers neither; a token that stops answering triggers only 002; a token that answers with 6.4MB triggers only 001. Different trigger, different mitigation, different reader.
flaggedForReview.resolution: SEPARATE. If a report-writer prefers one submission, 001 must appear as a named sub-section of it, never dropped.

flaggedForReview.item: CODE-204 merged into DEDUP-02-002 - the one merge in this run that is a judgement call
flaggedForReview.question: CODE-204 (honest token with a non-view decimals()) was merged as trigger T3 of DEDUP-02-002 rather than kept separate. Basis: identical root cause (annihilate hard-requires a static-callable decimals()), identical impact (fail-closed brick for that pair, before the burn), identical mitigation family (registration checklist + NatSpec scope). ECON-008's own attackScenario already enumerates a sibling trigger (a pre-metadata token with no decimals() at all), so the finding was already multi-trigger by construction.
flaggedForReview.residualDoubt: CODE-204's recommendation is documentation-only while ECON-008's adds an operational invariant. If the severity-classifier judges those distinct enough, SPLIT - the trigger inventory in DEDUP-02-002 preserves everything needed to do so cleanly and no evidence was discarded.
flaggedForReview.resolution: MERGED, reversibly, with the full trigger inventory retained.

flaggedForReview.item: PATTERN-001 mapped to M-03 alone, not to M-05, and not to both
flaggedForReview.question: The brief flagged this as a judgement call. M-03 = under-counting (one leg not charged to the cap); M-05 = budget contention (annihilation extracts 2x per unit of a shared budget, making on-ramp griefing profitable). PATTERN-001's text addresses only the former.
flaggedForReview.risk: If the classifier disagrees and reads PATTERN-001 as spanning both, the consequence is benign - both entries are already wont-fix and neither is closed by this run. The consequence of the OPPOSITE error (collapsing M-03 and M-05 into one) would be severe: it would retire a distinct live root cause under another's triage.
flaggedForReview.resolution: M-03 only. M-05 explicitly NOT closed, NOT re-filed, NOT collapsed; invariant_8 recorded against it as corroboration.

flaggedForReview.item: DEDUP-02-003 (CODE-201) kept OUT of ledger F-01
flaggedForReview.question: CODE-201's own text says 'This is ledger F-01'. It was nonetheless filed as a new QA entry because its substance is the MISLEADING FRAMING of a new guard, not the missing guard itself, and because its entire operational value is to prevent F-01 being closed on false evidence. Folding it into F-01 would make the tripwire invisible inside the finding it is meant to protect.
flaggedForReview.resolution: SEPARATE, with an explicit relatedNotCollapsed link and WATCH-02-02. If the classifier prefers, it may be rendered as a named sub-section of the F-01 write-up - but it must retain its own fingerprint so a future run can reconcile it independently.

flaggedForReview.item: DEDUP-02-008 severity - the impact inversion crosses a category boundary
flaggedForReview.question: L-01 was filed Low as a VALUE LEAK. It is now a LIVENESS lever proven by a passing PoC (one wei permanently bricks a pair). Both readings are Low, but for opposite reasons, and the classifier should confirm Low is still right for the DoS framing given the brick is permanent while the hook is live.
flaggedForReview.resolution: Low preserved (unanimous across three tiers). Flagged because the impact class changed, not because the tiers disagreed.
